pr_title: Glances: Add error handling for invalid sensor data
pr_body:
Added error handling by setting sensor state to `Unavailable` when the received data from glances does not match the expected type.

Background:
When glances sensor plugin is used, it creates a `temperature_hdd` sensor for every hdd entity discovered by the plugin.
This sensor is configured with device_class `temperature`, which expects a numerical value.
When the hdd's discovered by glances do not provide temperature information, the native value is set to strings such aus `NA`, `SLP` or `UNK`.
This leads to HA throwing an error, because the type mismatches, which prevents all glances sensors from updating (see #93417 ).

issue_context.title: Glances not updating values after 2022.5
issue_context.body:
### The problem

since upgrading to 2022.5. the glances-integration is not updating values as before.

It used to update at least each 5 min,, but now it is only updating sensors if i reload the integration



HA in container in unRaid, glances container, hdd-temp container

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.5.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.4.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Glances

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/glances/

### Diagnostics information

Background:
Did run nicolargo glances:3.3.0.2 on 2023.4, but that did not work on 2023.5, 
so have now updated to nicolargo/glances:latest-full

it is now updating sensor values, but only at reload of integration :(


did see an error on restart,, disabled the "glances_sda_temperature" and reload integration, but did not get new sensor-values after the actual reload. After a new restart - the same error is back :(
(sda is the flash-drive with unRaid OS,, and it is not reporting any temperature

review_comments: Every time we access `self.native_value` there's another `isinstance` check besides some dict lookups. I suggest storing the result the first time in a local variable for reuse.

Sounds like a good improvement, but the PR is already merged, so I am going to add it in another PR.
Dict lookups are not expensive at all with O(1) compared to the isinstance call. I think this can be neglected. I am not aware of the impact and performance hit of isinstance, but I agree that generally faster is better!
